In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fish enterocyte has the capacity to absorb and to extrude calcium.
the fish enterocyte presents a model for a cell in which Na+/ Ca2+ exchange is a major contributor to Ca2+ efflux.
the Na+/ Ca2+ exchanger, with high affinity for calcium, plays a significant role in Ca2+ extruding from the enterocyte.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ca2+ absorption via the fish intestinal epithelium is mediated by a sodium-coupled Ca2+ transport mechanism, which involves a Na+/Ca2+-exchange system and a Ca2+ pump.
Ca2+ absorption in the fish intestine is driven by a sodium gradient and is accomplished by the combined operation of ATP-dependent Ca2+-pump and Na+/Ca2+-exchanger.
calcium absorption in the fish intestine is mediated via a paracellular route and is dependent on sodium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Na+/H+ exchanger is a major player in the absorption of Ca2+ in the fish intestine, which has been confirmed by other researchers as well.
the Na+/ Ca2+ exchanger is an important contributor to the extrusion of Ca2+ in the fish intestine, and that this mechanism may be a general feature of the Ca2+ extruding machinery in fish cells.
the Na+/ Ca2+ exchange is the primary mechanism of Ca2+ extrusions in fish enterocyte.
